findings.title: What this is about
findings.answer: A pending regulated electric rate case for Pueblo, Cañon City, Rocky Ford and other customers in Black Hills Colorado Electric territory.

findings.title: Main finding
findings.answer: The proposed $26,663,479 annual revenue change is not a bill already approved. The 600-kWh example rises $18.30/month without the proposed temporary credit.

findings.title: History
findings.answer: The 2024 filing was ultimately reduced; March 2025 reporting describes $17M approved and roughly $7/month residential impact. The new application is separate.

findings.title: Current status
findings.answer: June 12 filing; Council opposition October 26; public comments in December and January. Applicant anticipates March 2027, regulator targets spring 2027; actual effective date depends on order.

findings.title: Dates
findings.answer: December 1 Cañon City; December 2 Pueblo; January 19, 2027 virtual. Early January is encouraged for written comments; confirm latest schedule.

findings.title: Affected people
findings.answer: Over 102,000 regional customer accounts per company notice, not 102,000 people or Pueblo-only households.

findings.title: Children
findings.answer: Higher energy costs could reduce disposable income for food, heating and education. No child-level outcomes have been measured.

findings.title: Families and workers
findings.answer: The example adds $130.80/year with credit or $219.60/year without it. Fixed-income burden depends on actual bills and income.

findings.title: Neighborhoods
findings.answer: Different rate territories and housing efficiencies matter. Compare usage-matched bills, not a Pueblo address label or one anecdote.

findings.title: Fairness
findings.answer: The proposed fixed charge rises from $8.77 to $12.00; assess low-usage and energy-burden impacts, including renters who cannot modify their homes.

findings.title: Responsibility
findings.answer: Black Hills files and operates the system; the Colorado PUC regulates tariffs; Pueblo City Council can oppose and participate but does not set the PUC rate.

findings.title: Decision makers
findings.answer: PUC determines the outcome; public comments inform the process. Trial staff and utility consumer advocate participate; docket index also lists city and county intervention motions.

findings.title: Rules
findings.answer: The proceeding reviews proposed tariffs and prudent recoverable costs. Obtain current procedural schedule, orders and testimony before assigning approval status.

findings.title: Commitments
findings.answer: Applicant reports approximately $184M invested since the last filing. The claim is not equivalent to a verified rate-base addition or an allowed return.

findings.title: Accountability
findings.answer: Request utility workpapers, approved revenue requirement, rate-base roll-forward, cost allocation, audit sampling, and service outcomes. Regulator's public docket is the first route; private company records are not automatically public records.

findings.title: Revenue
findings.answer: Proposed incremental annual revenue is a system-wide request, not profits, Pueblo-only receipts, or a tax.

findings.title: Household costs
findings.answer: 600-kWh filed baseline $124.18; temporary-credit example $135.08; no-credit example $142.48. Small commercial examples $277.47, $285.66, $303.99.

findings.title: Approved amounts
findings.answer: No final order for the new increase was established as of November 18. Do not substitute the company's requested rate or 2025 decision for the new outcome.

findings.title: Actual payments
findings.answer: No ledger of realized 2026–27 collections or individual work orders was reconciled. Request tariff-to-bill sample, actual capital invoices and recovery by account.

findings.title: Costs and benefits
findings.answer: Utility cites reliability, resilience and operating costs. Measure whether outage minutes, frequency, capacity and safety improve relative to demonstrated spending.

findings.title: How it works
findings.answer: Base charges, usage rates and riders interact. Proposal replaces two residential base-energy tiers (12.159 and 15.807 cents/kWh) with 16 cents/kWh, plus other charges and adjustments.

findings.title: Capacity
findings.answer: Company identifies Erie Avenue, Pueblo Industrial Park and airport generation infrastructure investments; actual spare distribution capacity is not established.

findings.title: Quality
findings.answer: Request annual SAIDI/SAIFI, outage causes, restoration performance and service-quality compliance, with comparable exclusions and years.

findings.title: Maintenance
findings.answer: Residents request location-specific vegetation trimming records. Request aggregated corridors, completed miles, dates, contractors, labor, actual versus budget, allocation and tariff recovery; redact security-sensitive detail.

findings.title: Obstacles
findings.answer: Court or regulatory disputes, capital cost, fuel prices, procurement and rate design may affect timelines. Do not infer future delay without procedural evidence.

findings.title: Connected issues
findings.answer: Municipal bills, schools, museums, nonprofits, hospitals, housing, public safety and small businesses could face operating-cost pressure. No citywide cost has been measured.

findings.title: Energy needs
findings.answer: Separate resource plan case 26A-0333E and economic development case 25A-0500E matter for future power demand and cost allocation. Avoid treating their dollars as additive without a model.

findings.title: Environment
findings.answer: Reliability, wildfire mitigation, fuel and renewable resources may carry distinct benefits and costs. Request quantified outcomes and alternatives, not a standalone claim that all spending is necessary.

findings.title: Risks
findings.answer: Credit expires; higher base persists if approved as filed. Rate shock can interact with rent, gas, water and insurance increases; no cascading insolvency forecast is established.

findings.title: Long term
findings.answer: Compare five- and twenty-year cumulative costs, affordability, debt, technology, reliability, and future grid investment under each provider scenario.

findings.title: Alternatives
findings.answer: Regulated incumbent with rate scrutiny, negotiated concessions, energy assistance, weatherization, community solar, cooperative or public-power feasibility, and regional bulk-power options. No immediate supplier switch is established.

findings.title: Tradeoffs
findings.answer: City-only utility draft puts acquisition-related total at $383–503M in 2030 dollars and finds city-only municipalization infeasible under assumptions. Black Hills-funded study estimates financing above $1B under its own framework; reconcile scopes rather than merge figures.

findings.title: Lessons
findings.answer: Benchmark Xcel, San Isabel Electric and Colorado Springs Utilities using current tariffs, identical usage, all riders, reliability and capitalization. No tariff-normalized ranking was verified here.

findings.title: Improvements
findings.answer: Publish a plain-language revenue bridge, maintenance accountability matrix, matched-tariff comparator, energy-burden dashboard and assistance navigator; assign review owners before implementation.

findings.title: Public action
findings.answer: Submit case 26AL-0232E comments and factual examples; ask for written answers. No need to disclose private bill account number in public filings.

findings.title: Evidence strength
findings.answer: Regulator confirms proposal and refund mechanics; utility notice supplies bill scenarios. Hearing specifics partly corroborated via local reporting/mayor. Official direct docket review remains incomplete.

findings.title: Conflicting claims
findings.answer: Rate approval is not inevitable: prior case was reduced. State statutes limit PUC mandates to remove gas appliances from existing buildings in relevant programs; check local/new-building rules separately. No proof of excess profit or maintenance fraud supplied.

findings.title: Unknowns
findings.answer: Current staff and intervenor positions, requested and allowed return on equity, actual vegetation cost and location data, rate-class allocation, city facility costs, and final order.

findings.title: Change triggers
findings.answer: New testimony, settlement, commission order, revised tariff, hearing changes, or a validated municipalization update trigger amendments; historical baseline stays intact.

findings.title: Qified insight
findings.answer: The temporary credit, permanent base-rate design, system costs and household outcomes must be tracked separately. Pair evidence-led intervention with source-backed local relief and long-term scenario comparisons.
